netWorth.caveat: This is not household net worth. It excludes the home — the asset the mortgage and HELOC are secured against — plus vehicles, pensions, the business, and the unquantified American Express. Household net worth cannot be stated until the home is valued.

helocSummary: Balance grew $7,536.96 over 18 months despite $78,177 of repayments, because $86,514 was advanced and $15,029 of interest was capitalised. Since the February 2026 paydown it has risen every month — +$13,525.55 in six.

cashflowNote: Nine of eighteen complete months were negative. The year balances only because two or three large months carry it. Excludes payments made directly from the HELOC — roughly $1,960/month — so the real picture is somewhat weaker than shown.
incomeNote: Her Tennis BC employment — 43 deposits, $63,129.47 over 18 months into DEBT&PAYMENTS — was absent from the earlier picture entirely, which saw only the $21,700 she transferred across. That transfer has been removed as an income line: it is an internal movement out of this income, and counting both would double it. Two cautions remain: at least $1,639.10 marked EXP is expense reimbursement rather than pay, a further $2,846.58 marked AP is unresolved, and the transfers stopped after May 2026 while the income did not.
spendingNote: Household spending averages about $7,551/month over 18 months. Roughly 19% could not be reliably categorised — TD truncates merchant names. This total is still incomplete: $9,930 of Amazon Mastercard purchases and $6,760 on the two TD Visas are captured but not yet folded into any category.
